statement: A position-based bound for the partition-internal tables _partition_statement_outcomes and _participant_transactions, tied to the snapshot boundary and applied inside apply, on the model of reclaimDeliveredCdcObligations for _cdc_obligations. Today _partition_statement_outcomes gains one row per committed statement in every partition, is carried in snapshots and has no DELETE; its own comment defers the bound to "the snapshot/log-bound quest". The bound must be the same on every replica at the same log position, and a retry arriving after the bound gets an explicit, ruled answer. Size L. Not sealable before the owner rules the retry-dedupe horizon.

constraints.statement: Reclamation is a deterministic function of the applied log position, executed inside apply, so every replica and every snapshot installer holds the same rows at the same position. No wall-clock expiry and no out-of-band delete.

A statement outcome is what makes a retried committed statement answer once. How long that guarantee holds is an owner ruling recorded in this log before the quest is sealed; past the horizon a retry gets a named outcome (R07), never a silent second execution.

A _participant_transactions row is retired only after its transaction is terminal on this participant and no recovery, settlement or coordinator query can still need it; coordinate that predicate with transaction-table-retention, one writer per interaction.

The bound is tied to the snapshot boundary through the snapshot owner's contract (src/raft snapshot checkpoint and application content); the quest does not invent a second definition of the boundary. Whether follower Raft logs are compacted was not established by the census and is established here before the bound is designed.

sweepExpiredReservations (src/partition/partition-locking-read-reservation.js) deletes expired rows of the partition-internal _lagrange_locking_read_reservations table by wall clock and has no production caller. It is wired by the owner of that table or deleted (no-legacy rule); if it is wired, the quest first establishes whether that table is replicated state, because a wall-clock delete on replicated state is refused by position-based-inside-apply.

A table moves out of class unbounded in solve/epics/system-table-retention/table-lifetimes.json only in the change that lands its retention owner, and the retained entry names that owner as file:symbol. The declaration is never edited to lower the epic metric ahead of the code.
The src/ changes land only behind an approving verification newer than the last attempt.
